subject: Stream SLA sampling scope & crest vs sustained sizing
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@shiply.com>, Ava Liao <ava.liao@shiply.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Dec 2028 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Stream SLA sampling scope & crest vs sustained sizing

Hi Samir / Ava — thanks again for the call this morning. High-level recap and proposed next steps so we have an aligned scope for Redwood's sizing and telemetry sampling work: 

Recap (what you told us)
- Primary product: in-chat logistics assistant that streams partial responses for ETA estimation and follow-ups.
- Steady-state traffic: ~2.5k QPS across the fleet, ~8k tokens/sec aggregate (mostly short chunks, median 40 tokens).
- Crest episodes: marketing-triggered 'delivery blitz' produces short 60–120s crest windows; crest observed historically hits ~60k tokens/sec aggregate and ~14k QPS for 45–90s.
- Latency targets (customer SLO aspirations): 95th percentile first-token <= 200ms, per-chunk tail (99th) <= 120ms for streaming.
- Important constraints: prefix caching expected to cover ~30–40% of requests; KV cache warmups during crests are a risk.

Primary asks from Redwood after today's sync
1) Confirm crest definition and historical frequency: provide 2 weeks of traces (we asked for 2x crest windows and 5 representative steady windows).
2) Export a 1-hour sample around a crest (ndjson trace preferred) so we can run synthetic replays against our continuous-batching simulation.
3) Share a representative request size distribution (tokens per chunk and total tokens per session).
4) Call out any hard latency caps (e.g., network-side timeouts) and whether you can tolerate model-variant fallback during crests.

What Redwood will deliver (initial)
- A sizing note that maps: steady-state -> recommended reserved concurrency and batching targets; crest -> temporary burst policy and graceful-fallback plan.
- Telemetry sampling plan: a deterministic sampling recipe to capture crest tail behavior (higher sampling during crest windows + adaptive trace rate to keep ingestion within your SI limits).
- Quick simulation report showing expected 95/99 latency ranges under current cache-hit assumptions (we'll publish two scenarios: 35% cache hits and 10% cache hits).

Immediate next steps / owners
- Samir: share the two crest-hour ndjson traces and a CSV with tokens-per-request distribution by EOD Wednesday. (owner: Samir)
- Mina: produce a one-page sizing sketch and sampling plan by Friday (owner: Mina).
- Marissa & Jordan: technical review of the simulation assumptions and recommended burst policy (owners: Marissa, Jordan).

Attachments: streaming_sample_plan.xlsx (basic fields we need filled), example_trace_20281203.ndjson (format example).

If the crest duration or peak numbers above don't match your instrumentation, please flag — I'll adjust. Happy to schedule a 30-min replay run with engineering if you want a live handoff.

Thanks,
Mina
--
Mina Haddad
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Samir Patel <samir@shiply.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ava Liao <ava.liao@shiply.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Dec 2028 11:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Stream SLA sampling scope & crest vs sustained sizing

Thanks Mina — that aligns well with what we saw. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Crest duration: our observations vary; the most severe ones are 40–90s with a mean around 65s. We have two clear crest events in the attached week — I'll push those ndjson files to the Drive link you shared.
- Burst origin: 70% of crest calls come from a single campaign cluster (eu-west), 30% are organic. Could that affect routing/fallback decisions?
- Cache behavior: prefix cache is spotty on crests because many of the campaign prompts have dynamic IDs; effective cache hit drops to ~8% during crests.

Two quick asks for Redwood: 
1) Can you include an explicit 'cold-kv' scenario (0–5% cache) in the simulation? That will be the realistic worst-case for us.
2) What's the recommended token-conservative fallback? We want to avoid hallucinations but are willing to accept shorter chunks in 30% of crest traffic.

I'll upload the sample traces and the token distribution CSV by EOD Wednesday. If you want, Ava and I can be on the quick replay call.

Samir
Shiply — Head of Platform
samir@shiply.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 3 Dec 2028 13:00:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Stream SLA sampling scope & crest vs sustained sizing

Internal notes / proposed technical approach before we create the formal sizing doc: 

1) Simulation parameters to run (two scenarios):
   - Nominal: steady-state 2.5k QPS, avg tokens/req = 40, cache hit 35%, model variant = rw-medium-fp16, batching window = 6ms target, concurrency per GPU = 32.
   - Worst (crest cold-kv): crest peak 14k QPS, avg tokens/req = 55 (campaign prompts), cache hit = 8%, model variant = rw-small-q4, burst policy = preemptive routing to dedicated burst pool with 2x concurrency, aggressive batching window = 12ms to increase throughput.

2) Measurements to produce: token/sec and tokens-per-second-per-GPU, per-chunk latency CDFs (50/95/99), and modeled request-drop or fallback rates under two fallback options (shorter chunk + smaller model).

3) Telemetry sampling plan (brief):
   - During normal windows: deterministic 0.2% trace sampling, plus 1% error sampling.
   - During crest detection (traffic delta > 4x baseline sustained for 30s): switch to stratified sampling: 5% across random requests, 100% of requests that hit 99th latency buckets, and all requests that trigger fallback.

4) Deliverables and SWAT tasks:
   - Mina: draft sizing note + sampling plan (Friday).
   - Jordan: set up replay harness and synthetic crest runner (ETA Thursday).
   - Marissa: run simulations and produce latency CDFs (ETA next Tuesday).

I'll drop a minimal template into the Drive folder (the spreadsheet Mina attached). Also recommend we include a quick smoke test using rw-medium-fp16 with 0.5s per-session duration to validate the queueing model.

-Marissa
VP, Performance Ops (Redwood)
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Stream SLA sampling scope & crest vs sustained sizing

Samir / Ava — thanks, this is helpful. Quick consolidated plan and proposal for signoff so we can proceed with simulations this week: 

1) You (Shiply) to provide: two crest-hour ndjson exports + 5 steady 10-minute windows (CSV / ndjson) + tokens-per-request histogram by Wednesday EOD. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cStreamSamples
2) Redwood to produce by Friday: one-page sizing sketch, simulation CDFs (50/95/99), and the telemetry sampling recipe (spreadsheet attached). We will publish two scenarios (nominal and worst-cold-kv).
3) Fallback options we will evaluate:
   - Option A: shorter chunk length (reduce avg tokens/req by ~30%) + rw-medium-fp16; expected lower latency but slightly higher model cost.
   - Option B: model-variant fallback to rw-small-q4 with prefix checks, applied to 30% of crest traffic; cheaper but potential quality delta.

Please reply with a single-line approval if Shiply is okay with Redwood running crest replay simulations with your traces and marking samples with IP-port anonymization. If you want us to redact anything before upload, flag the files and we'll coordinate.

I'll attach the spreadsheet now (streaming_sample_plan.xlsx) and upload the example ndjson format for your trace team. If everyone's aligned I'll schedule a 30-min handoff replay on Thursday 11am PT (tentative).

Best,
Mina
